evidence.curator_note: Equation 8.37, line 1 of 3: 'OE+.  AB(+)CD  --sigma-->  AB. + CD+  or  AB+ + .CD'. Generic sigma-bond dissociation of an odd-electron (OE+.) molecular ion: the central C-C sigma bond, drawn carrying the '+' (a 2-centre/1-electron loose sigma bond in the radical cation, per the text 'On dissociation of such a weakened C-C sigma-bond, one of the carbon atoms will bear the charge, and the other will bear the radical site'), homolyses. Either fragment can retain the charge (the 'or': AB.+CD+ vs AB++.CD), the balance set by bond polarization / Stevenson's Rule. ARC COUNT (convention D): the book draws 0 curved arrows/fishhooks - equation 8.37 is a net reactant->products scheme written with a straight sigma-labelled reaction arrow, not an arrow-pushing diagram. The 2 encoded electron_moves are IMPLICIT (reconstructed for electron balance, not drawn): move <1> routes one electron of the cleaving C2-C3 sigma bond OUT of the system (external = the EI ionization hole, since the drawn skeleton is neutral and the +/. live in the fields), move <2> routes the other C2-C3 electron onto C2 to make the ethyl radical; C3 is left electron-deficient -> ethyl cation. This is the delocalized-bond localization convention used for pure-hydrocarbon sigma dissociation in IMS4-EQ4.3. INSTANTIATION (convention F): the scheme is generic (A,B,C,D undefined; NO m/z or intensity printed). Instantiated as the n-BUTANE radical cation cleaving the central C2-C3 bond - the very bond the text singles out ('in the butane cation the lowest-energy structure has a very long C(2)-C(3) bond, 2.02 A'). Butane's C2-C3 cleavage is SYMMETRIC, so both polarizations of the 'or' give the same product pair (ethyl cation + ethyl radical); this single record therefore covers both branches. Curator-computed detected ion m/z 29.0386 (C2H5+); this derives from the chosen instantiation, not from the page. LOCALIZATION (convention B): charge/radical are carried in the species fields against a neutral butane skeleton rather than drawn on a specific atom, because the book localizes the '+' on the sigma BOND (a 2c-1e species) which has no valence-correct single-atom SMILES form.

NO MOD rule is indexed for Equation 8.37 (rule_index.json 'by_equation' has entries only through 8.14; there is no 8.37 key). No cross-link is asserted. The mechanistically analogous chapter-4 sigma dissociation of propane (Eq 4.3, records IMS4-EQ4.3a/b) is encoded by MOD variables IMS_4_3_var1/var2, but those are keyed to 4.3, not to this equation, and describe propane rather than butane. m/z 29.0386 (C2H5+) is curator-computed from the R=butane instantiation because the page prints no m/z and no intensity.
